L3.1.quote: When the players alternately select pieces of a fixed multiset \(L\), Liu Bang first, Liu Bang's optimal total equals \(V(L)=\frac12\Bigl(\sum L+D(L)\Bigr)\). (The optimum is realised by always selecting a currently longest remaining piece.)
L3.1.note: Reduction correctly stated and used throughout, but asserted without any proof.

L3.2.quote: Let \(L\) be an arbitrary finite multiset of nonnegative reals with \(\sum L=S_n=2^{n+1}-1\). There exists a refinement of \(L\) obtained by adding at most \(n\) cuts such that the resulting multiset \(M\) satisfies \(D(M)\le 1\).
L3.2.note: Theorem stated; proof self-contradictory and garbled; dyadic-pairing cut-count claim unjustified; only n≤2 checked; pigeonhole/mirroring absent.

L3.3.quote: Any multiset obtained from \(B_n\) by performing at most \(n\) cuts satisfies \(D\ge 1\). Consequently the after-cut multiset \(M\) of the scaled stick obeys \(V(M)=\frac{S+D(M)}{2}\ge\frac{S+1}{2}=2^n\), and on the original stick Liu Bang obtains at least \(2^n/S\).
L3.3.note: Construction correct; base case and k=0 case valid; k≥1 subcases broken (padding arithmetic wrong, virtual-cut argument incomplete, appeals to numerics).

parsed.notes: Correct final answer stated. Reduction asserted unproven. Lower-bound induction fails for k≥1 (erroneous padding, numerical appeals). Upper-bound proof contradicts itself; dyadic pairing cut-count unjustified; small-n checks only. Neither bound validly established for all n.
